newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees risk of rising trade surpluses.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees risk of rising trade surpluses.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Monday that he saw a risk of rising trade surpluses in some industrial nations and called on those countries to promote domestic demand and open markets.

"Where there is a risk of rising external surpluses, it is appropriate that policies be directed at achieving domestic demand-led growth as well as measures to open markets," Rubin told the International Monetary Fund's Interim Committee.
Rubin did not specify any countries by name, but in the past he and other U.S. officials have warned Japan to avoid a significant rise in its current account surplus.

Rubin took encouragement from the economic outlook in many countries and said he was particularly pleased that the U.S. expansion had been led by strong business investment. "(That) bodes well for our ability to maintain strong growth rates without encountering capacity constraints," he said.
Inflation has remained low in advanced countries for several years and "there appears now to be little risk of a resurgence of inflation," Rubin added.
"Financial markets have responded favorably to the healthy macroeconomic performance and significant structural reforms of the past year ... Yet many challenges remain," he said.

"In the emerging markets, we should all view with caution the risks posed by large current account deficits, high concentrations of short-term debt, weak financial systems and inflexible exchange rates," Rubin said.

"While these conditions may have been sustainable in the relatively benign global interest rate and financial environment of the past year or two, they may not be sustainable in different circumstances," he added.
He also stressed the importance of pressing ahead with trade liberalization.
